LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard metadata variables (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, etc.) and uses a `source` array pointing to the expected upstream Git repository. The only executable code in the global scope is within the `pkgver()` function, which is not executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`—it will only run later during the build process. At parse time, sourcing the PKGBUILD only evaluates static variable assignments and array definitions, none of which involve command substitution, network operations, or file system modifications. There are no top-level commands or dangerous variable expansions that would trigger execution when printing srcinfo.

The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is normal for VCS-based packages and does not pose a risk during this phase, as no sources are downloaded or verified. While the use of an unpinned Git branch in `source` could affect reproducibility, it does not enable arbitrary code execution at parse time. No obfuscated code, data exfiltration, or remote execution mechanisms are present in the global scope.

Thus, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe, as it only parses declarative package metadata without invoking any active commands.
</details>
<evidence>

No active code in global scope; safe to parse
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>

<details>
The provided <.SRCINFO> file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It declares standard fields such as package name, description, version, architecture, dependencies, source location, and checksums. The source is set to a Git repository over HTTPS from GitHub (https://github.com/bschaatsbergen/cidr.git), which aligns with the declared upstream URL. This is normal for -git packages in the AUR.

The `sha256sums = SKIP` entry is expected for VCS-based packages where the source is a Git repository, as the content is inherently mutable and cannot be checksummed in the traditional sense. This practice is well-documented and acceptable in the AUR ecosystem. No executable code or scripts are present in this file — it only contains packaging metadata. There are no signs of obfuscation, unauthorized network operations, or malicious payloads.

All declared dependencies (`go`, `glibc`) are appropriate for a Go-compiled CLI tool targeting multiple architectures. The license (MIT) matches typical open-source expectations. There is no evidence of supply-chain tampering, backdoors, or data exfiltration mechanisms.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard AUR package for a Go-based CLI tool that handles CIDR notation. It fetches the source from the project's official GitHub repository using a git+https URL, which is appropriate for a -git package. The sha256sums value is set to 'SKIP', which is expected and normal for VCS-based packages where content changes frequently; this is not a security issue in this context.

The build process consists of standard, safe operations: `go build` with `-trimpath` and `-buildvcs=false` for reproducibility, followed by `make test` in the check() function. The package() function installs only the built binary, the license, and documentation to appropriate system directories. All actions are confined to the build directory and target package directory, with no network access or external side effects during packaging.

There are no signs of obfuscation, unauthorized downloads, data exfiltration, or execution of untrusted code. The operations align with standard AUR packaging practices for a -git package. While the source uses a mutable git reference (which reduces reproducibility), this is common and not inherently malicious, especially when the source is the official upstream.
</details>
